items.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had D. Sharp as a drummer for many years

ctx.x: So were you going through, as you were bringing musicians in, you were thinking about what they brought to the table? Or was it a discovery once they came in the band?

Sometimes it would be a shock. Like if all of a sudden Gary Valente pulled out of the Japanese tour and got Ray Anderson instead. That music was not written for him. Those two trombone players were totally different. So that’s a disadvantage now if you write for one person and all of a sudden they can’t show up or don’t show up. You’re giving someone else their music, and it doesn’t sometimes work out for the musician or for the arranger. But mostly I just kept everybody all the time. And eventually, Steve made…
[Laughs] Yeah, yeah the old greenback does do magic there.
